run.question: b4-demo 这个 namespace 的服务为什么起不来

report.summary: In namespace b4-demo the only workload is Deployment web (Helm release web, chart web 0.1.0). Its pod template now specifies the image nginx:does-not-exist-b4, which does not exist in the registry: the pod of the new ReplicaSet web-d59578599 stays Pending with ImagePullBackOff and the exact kubelet error "failed to pull and unpack image docker.io/library/nginx:does-not-exist-b4 ... not found". That is why the new revision cannot start. Helm revision 3 (last deployed 2026-11-20T21:39:21Z) is recorded as failed with "resource Deployment/b4-demo/web not ready ... context deadline exceeded". Counter-evidence: the Service web still has one ready endpoint (10.244.0.46 -> pod web-b77b9fdb5-gj4jq, image nginx:1.27.4), which is serving HTTP 200 to kube-probe, so the previously deployed version is still answering; only the new revision's pod is blocked.

claims.text: Deployment web in namespace b4-demo has spec.template container image nginx:does-not-exist-b4, spec.replicas 1, generation 3 with observedGeneration 3, readyReplicas 1, and conditions MinimumReplicasAvailable and ReplicaSetUpdated.

Pod web-d59578599-m8mlm is Pending, its container web is not ready and waiting with reason ImagePullBackOff, message "Back-off pulling image \"nginx:does-not-exist-b4\": ErrImagePull: rpc error: code = NotFound desc = failed to pull and unpack image \"docker.io/library/nginx:does-not-exist-b4\": ... not found".

Events for pod web-d59578599-m8mlm record reason Failed (type Warning) at 2026-11-20T21:42:27Z: "Failed to pull image \"nginx:does-not-exist-b4\" ... docker.io/library/nginx:does-not-exist-b4: not found" and "Error: ErrImagePull", each counted 5 times.

All three ReplicaSets of Deployment web are owned by Deployment web: web-685fcc95d4 (image nginx:1.27.3, desired 0), web-b77b9fdb5 (image nginx:1.27.4, desired 1, ready 1) and web-d59578599 (image nginx:does-not-exist-b4, desired 1, ready null/unset).

Deployment web emitted a ScalingReplicaSet rollout sequence inside the window: scale up web-685fcc95d4 at 21:39:15Z, scale up web-b77b9fdb5 at 21:39:16Z, scale down web-685fcc95d4 to 0 and scale up web-d59578599 at 21:39:21Z, all Normal events.

Helm release web in b4-demo has revision 1 (Install complete, 21:39:15Z), revision 2 (Upgrade complete, 21:39:16Z) and revision 3 status failed, last deployed 2026-11-20T21:39:21Z, description "Upgrade \"web\" failed: resource Deployment/b4-demo/web not ready. status: InProgress, message: Pending termination: 1 context deadline exceeded".

The old pod is still healthy and serving: Endpoints web lists address 10.244.0.46 for pod web-b77b9fdb5-gj4jq (notReadyAddresses contains only 10.244.0.47 for web-d59578599-m8mlm), and pod web-b77b9fdb5-gj4jq (image nginx:1.27.4) is ready with container state running since 21:39:20Z, logging HTTP 200 responses to kube-probe/1.37 from 21:39:31Z through 21:42:46Z. The namespace is therefore not wholly down; only the new revision's pod cannot start.

Rejected as the cause of the current failure: readiness-probe "connection refused" misses. The only Unhealthy events are single startup-time readiness probe failures on web-685fcc95d4-cz4tq (21:39:15Z) and web-b77b9fdb5-gj4jq (21:39:20Z); web-685fcc95d4 was then deleted by the rollout (SuccessfulDelete, 21:39:21Z) and web-b77b9fdb5-gj4jq is now ready and answering probes with HTTP 200.

Namespace b4-demo contains exactly one Deployment (web), one Service (web, clusterIP 10.96.156.106, port 80, selector app.kubernetes.io/instance=web, app.kubernetes.io/name=web) and one ConfigMap (kube-root-ca.crt); no other workload in the namespace was found to be failing.

Rejected as unrelated to b4-demo: the single Endpoints/FailedToCreateEndpoint event at 2026-11-20T21:26:40Z belongs to service loki in namespace app-101 ("endpoints \"loki\" already exists"), a different namespace and service, and no evidence ties it to Deployment web or Service web.

The exact failure text shows the image reference is unresolvable, not a scheduling, resource, probe or policy problem: the kubelet reports docker.io/library/nginx:does-not-exist-b4 "not found", the pod is scheduled on opspilot-m1-control-plane (Scheduled 21:39:21Z) and no Evicted/OOMKilled/Failed container termination appears for it.

gaps: The Helm chart values or the source of the image tag nginx:does-not-exist-b4 could not be read (helm_list/helm_history/helm_status return release metadata only, not values), so it cannot be verified whether the tag came from a chart value, an override, or a manual edit; no ConfigMap in b4-demo holds an image setting (only kube-root-ca.crt was readable).

Objects reflect the cluster state at query time (21:42-21:43Z); events inside the authorized window start at 2026-11-20T21:39:15Z, so whether the Deployment pod template differed before 21:39:15Z is unknown.

Helm secrets/chart manifests could not be read, so the exact revision content that introduced nginx:does-not-exist-b4 is unverified beyond the failed revision 3 record and the observed rollout events.
Whether the registry would accept this tag under different credentials was not checked; only the kubelet pull error (NotFound) is observed.
next_steps: Roll back the Helm release to revision 2 (helm rollback web 2 -n b4-demo) or set the Deployment/values image back to the known-good nginx:1.27.4, then confirm a new ReplicaSet's pod becomes Ready.
Verify the intended image tag exists in the registry before the next upgrade, and add a pre-upgrade check so a NotFound tag does not leave the release in failed state.
Confirm whether the invalid tag was introduced intentionally (fault-injection test) and record the source (values file or override) so the release values can be corrected.

view.cannot_prove: Release history is the current content of Helm's records: revisions outside the authorized window are listed too, so it cannot prove that only these changes happened inside the window. Only Helm's own record: changes made with kubectl apply or kubectl edit, or by any tool other than Helm, are not in it. Revision times come from Helm, not from when Pods finished rolling out; deployed only means Helm considered the release successful, not that its Pods are healthy.

Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). <none> means the path reached no value in that object, not that the field is absent from the kind; a filtered table is not a full picture of the kind.
